definitions.explanation: A child who has no siblings.

examples.japanese: ⟦{私|わたし}→私：02988_watashi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{一人|ひとり}っ{子|こ}です。
{一人|ひとり}っ{子|こ}だ⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{兄弟|きょうだい}→兄弟：00964_kyoudai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ほしかった。
examples.english: Since I'm an only child, I wanted siblings.

examples.japanese: ⟦{最近|さいきん}→最近：00881_saikin⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{一人|ひとり}っ{子|こ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{家庭|かてい}→家庭：12315_katei⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{増|ふ}えている→増える：01183_fueru⟧。
examples.english: Families with only children are increasing recently.

notes:
{一人|ひとり}っ{子|こ} refers to a child with no siblings. The っ{子|こ} suffix gives a colloquial, familiar tone.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {一人|ひとり}っ{子|こ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{育|そだ}つ→育つ：01951_sodatsu⟧: to grow up as an only child
- {一人|ひとり}っ{子|こ}⟦{政策|せいさく}→政策：10070_seisaku⟧: one-child policy (China)

CULTURAL NOTE:
With Japan's declining birth rate (⟦{少子化|しょうしか}→少子化：04807_shoushika⟧), {一人|ひとり}っ{子|こ} families have become increasingly common. There is a common stereotype that only children are spoiled (⟦{甘|あま}やかされている→甘やかす：06625_amayakasu⟧) or selfish, though this is often inaccurate.

VARIANT:
{一人子|ひとりご} is a more formal/literary alternative.
